immediate.title: Stop all contact and payments
immediate.detail: Do not reply, click further links, or send any more money. If a transfer is in progress, try to cancel it.

immediate.title: Contact your bank or card provider now
immediate.detail: Call the number on the back of your card. Ask them to stop or dispute payments and to protect your accounts. Fast reporting improves the chance of recovery.

immediate.title: Secure your accounts
immediate.detail: Change passwords for any affected accounts, turn on two-factor authentication, and check for changes to recovery email or phone numbers.

immediate.title: Preserve the evidence
immediate.detail: Take screenshots and keep messages, emails, phone numbers, payment references, and web addresses before deleting anything.

immediate.title: Report to the right authority
immediate.detail: Use the official channel for your country below. Reporting helps investigators and warns others, even if you did not lose money.

platforms.name: Your bank or card provider
platforms.detail: Use the fraud number on your card or in your banking app to stop payments, dispute charges, and freeze compromised cards.

platforms.name: Email providers
platforms.detail: Use the built-in "Report phishing" or "Report spam" option in Gmail, Outlook, or Apple Mail so the provider can act on the sender.

platforms.name: Social media platforms
platforms.detail: Report fake profiles, hacked accounts, and scam ads through the in-app report tools on Instagram, Facebook, X, TikTok, and others.

platforms.name: Marketplaces
platforms.detail: Report scam buyers and sellers to eBay, Facebook Marketplace, or the relevant platform so they can remove accounts and listings.

platforms.name: Mobile networks
platforms.detail: Forward scam SMS messages to your carrier's spam-reporting short code (7726 in many countries) to help block numbers.

platforms.name: App stores
platforms.detail: Report fraudulent or fleeceware apps to the Apple App Store or Google Play so they can be reviewed and removed.

afterReport.title: Watch for follow-up 'recovery' scams
afterReport.detail: Fraudsters target people who have already lost money by posing as recovery agents, lawyers, or investigators who can 'get it back' for a fee. This is a second scam, ignore it.

afterReport.title: Monitor your accounts and credit
afterReport.detail: Check statements for unfamiliar activity and consider a credit freeze or fraud alert with the credit bureaus if your identity may be exposed.

afterReport.title: Keep your report reference
afterReport.detail: Save any case or reference number. Your bank or insurer may ask for it, and it links future information to your case.

afterReport.title: Tell people you trust
afterReport.detail: Sharing what happened removes stigma and helps friends and family recognise the same scam. Reporting is never something to be ashamed of.
